title: Go test outcomes are keyed by the IDs in each test's own name and ordered by ID
when: ReadOutcomes reads go test -json output with a subtest that carries two IDs and fails, a subtest whose name holds a slash, a subtest with an ID whose own subtest is skipped, tests with no ID, and words that look like IDs but are not, such as ST-STD-TRUST-R04. Then it reads output in which a name holds ST-FIX-INV01-T-holds or ST-FIX-SP05-Tx, a test record ID that goes on with a hyphen or a lower-case letter, in a Go test and in a Python subtest.
then: There is one outcome per ID, in ID order, with its result, its duration and the failure output as its detail. The tests with no ID and the words that are not IDs give no outcome. The run starts at the first event and finishes at the last. Each output with a malformed ID is refused, and the refusal names the word.

title: Python test outcomes are keyed by the IDs in each subtest's description
when: ReadOutcomes reads the Python runner's document with two subtests that carry IDs, not in ID order, and test methods that carry none. Then it reads documents with a result that is not passed, failed or skipped, with another format, or with no content, and go test output that is not JSON.
then: The two subtests give their outcomes in ID order, and the methods give none. Each bad document is refused.

title: The Python runner counts only a real pass as passed, and names each subtest by its description
when: The Python runner runs a suite with a passing, a failing and a skipped subtest that carry IDs, a method marked as an expected failure that fails, and a method marked as an expected failure whose subtest passes.
then: The subtests are passed, failed with the assertion as detail, and skipped with the reason, each by its description. The expected failure is skipped, not passed. The unexpected success is failed, for the method and for its subtest. Every result is passed, failed or skipped.

title: The go test -json output of two Go modules, one after the other in one file, reads as one run
when: ReadOutcomes reads one file that holds the go test -json output of two Go modules, one after the other, as the proof run writes the root module's output and then Assuring's modules': each module has a package of its own and a test of the same name, the second module has an ID of its own, and both carry one ID, which passes in the first and fails in the second. It reads the file with the root module first, and then with the second module first.
then: Both files give the same outcomes: one per ID from both modules, in ID order, and the ID that both carry is failed, with the second module's failure as its detail. The run starts at the first event of either module and finishes at the last.

title: The coverage at a commit is read from lathe check on that commit's tree alone, summed over every domain and kind, and two readings agree
when: With a git repository whose spec has three invariants of a domain and a constraint of the product, at two commits whose files differ, and a working tree that differs from both: MeasureCoverage runs the real Lathe CLI at the first commit twice, at the second commit once, at a short commit ID, and at a third commit whose spec has errors because the tests' file is gone. Then MeasureCoverage runs a stand-in Lathe that prints a reason on its standard output and another on its standard error and exits 2, and the real Lathe at a commit whose lathe.config.json says schema 2.
then: Each reading gives the counts of that commit's tree, summed over the domain and the product, and the standing of each obligation there; the working tree changes nothing. The two readings of the first commit are the same bytes. The short commit ID is refused. The commit with errors gives no measurement and a SpecError that names each error Lathe finds, never an empty coverage. Each run where Lathe exits non-zero gives a SpecError that holds what Lathe printed on both streams, its standard output cut at a limit, so the schema mismatch is named.

title: The coverage sums Lathe's counts over every domain and kind, and output whose gaps disagree with its counts is refused
when: readLatheCheck reads lathe check JSON with two domains, the product's own scope, three obligation kinds and gaps that are not shares. Then it reads output with a gap that the counts do not hold, gaps in another word, an obligation with no chain or two, a count above the total, no product, and text that is not JSON. Last, it reads the real output of Lathe 5, whose kinds carry their complexity and whose coverage scopes carry their debt.
then: The coverage is the sum of every scope and kind, and each obligation's standing follows its gaps: built only when designed. Each other output is refused, so a misread gap never counts an obligation. Lathe 5's output is read: 4 obligations, 4 designed, 2 built, 2 proved, as DS02-T01 measures the same commit.

title: The tree of a commit is written only inside its folder, and a link that leads out of it is refused
when: writeTree writes trees built with git mktree: a link to a folder outside and a folder of the same name with a file in it, a link to an absolute path, a link whose text leaves the tree, and a link that leaves the tree through another link. Then it writes a tree with a link to a file inside it.
then: Each of the first four trees is refused, and nothing is written outside the folder. The last tree is written, with its link as a link.

title: A pattern rule counts once in each domain that follows its pattern, with its standing in that domain, as Lathe counts it
when: With a git repository whose spec has two domains that follow one pattern with one rule, and a pattern rule test that proves the rule in one domain only: MeasureCoverage runs the real Lathe CLI at that commit, then at a commit that removes the pattern rule test and its test file; holdsRatchet compares the two measurements. Then readLatheCheck reads output whose scope lists a pattern rule that has no chain.
then: The first measurement agrees with Lathe's counts and holds the rule once for each domain, named with its domain: designed, built and proved in the domain with the test, designed and built in the other. At the second commit the rule falls from proved in that domain alone, and the ratchet gives one reason that names the rule with its domain. The output with no chain for the rule is refused.

title: A proof run attestation from GitHub's store verifies against the Sigstore trust root, and any altered part yields no attestation
when: VerifyAttestation fetches by the commit a real bundle from a store and checks it with SigstoreVerifier against the trust root of its day, at the change's own reference refs/pull/24/merge. Then it checks the bundle with the payload, the signature, the certificate, the inclusion proof or the log entry changed, with no log entry, against another trust root, for another commit, as no bundle and as text that is not JSON. Then a store gives a forged, the true and an empty bundle, and then the true bundle for another pull request's reference.
then: The store is asked for the commit. The true bundle gives a proof run about the commit with its 239 outcomes, change grade, signed by proof-run.yml at refs/pull/24/merge, at rekor:3614924958. Each altered bundle gives nothing at all and one refusal. With the three bundles, the true one is taken and the two others are refused. At another pull request's reference, no proof run is taken. The certificate of the true bundle names the commit its signing run ran at.

title: Of several verified proof runs the release-grade one and then the newest is taken in any order, and a store that cannot answer is an error
when: VerifyAttestation reads, through a signature check that stands for Sigstore's, a store that gives two change-grade proof runs, a release-grade one and a forged one, in two orders; then only the two change-grade ones, in two orders; then a statement whose predicate is not a whole proof run; then a store that cannot answer, a store with no attestation, and a short commit ID.
then: Each order gives the release-grade proof run with its own outcome, and the forged one is refused; with no release-grade one, the newest by its log entry. The broken predicate gives no proof run. The store that cannot answer and the short commit ID give an error; the empty store gives no proof run and no refusal.

title: The code faults of a commit come from its tree and spec alone, keyed and ordered, and two readings agree
when: Commits a tree with faults of five rules to a git repository and reads its faults from git objects; changes the working tree and reads the same commit again; then commits a change that takes one of three domains from a package, renames a record's missing identifier to another missing one, and reaches the same package through another package of no domain, and reads the new commit.
then: Expects one fault per rule and key, in rule then key order; the same faults from both readings of the first commit, whatever the working tree holds; and at the second commit the same faults with the same keys, the R01, R02 and R03 faults each with another reason.

title: The SBOMs are the same bytes from the same record and name each module of it
when: With a build record with a local main module, a remote module and a replaced module: WriteSBOMs runs twice; then on a record with one module version changed, on no record, and on a record whose modules are out of order.
then: The two runs give the same SPDX, then CycloneDX bytes, each naming the executable digest and each module by its package URL, the replaced module by its replacement; the changed record gives other bytes; no record and the unordered record are refused.

title: An executable whose digest, size, build settings or modules differ from the record is refused, and each is named
when: With a build record and what was found in an executable that matches it: the check runs; then the digest, the size, two build settings and the compiled modules differ.
then: The matching executable passes. The changed one is refused, and the check names the recorded and the found digest and size, each setting that differs or is extra or missing, and the module the record does not list.

title: A source snapshot is refused on any changed, missing or added file, and each is named
when: With the files a record lists: the check runs on the same files; then on files where one changed, one lost its executable bit, one is missing and one is added.
then: The same files pass. The changed files are refused, and the check names each of the four paths with what differs, and no path that matches.
notes: The image half of ST-BLD-DS02 is ST-BLD-DS02-T03.

title: An image is refused when any digest its record names differs
when: With an image layout that matches its record: An extra file or link, changed config bytes, a missing blob, a wrong application or CA digest, a wrong diff ID, a dirty packer or a duplicate index key.
then: VerifyImage refuses each with its own reason.

title: Each component generator returns the same files for the same inputs
when: With the ten plans of each built-in archetype that ST-STD-GEN-R03-T01 makes: Compares the generator files of the plans, without main.go and go.mod.
then: Expects the same files with the same content in every plan.
notes: Not proof yet, for the same reason as ST-STD-GEN-R03-T01: 16 of the 26 components are not reached. That the generator receives only its context is shown by ST-STD-GEN-R01-T01 and ST-STD-GEN-R02-T01.

title: The assembler writes the same main.go and go.mod for the same wirings
when: With the ten plans of each built-in archetype that ST-STD-GEN-R03-T01 makes: Compares main.go and go.mod across the plans.
then: Expects the same content in every plan.
notes: One assembler serves every archetype, and the three archetypes give it wirings with routes, middleware, processes and a database.
